title: "Whiteboards on Start + Void"
description: "The dedicated Whiteboards Worker: profiles, build, the held cutover steps, smoke checks and rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-11-25"
audience: developers
---

`apps/whiteboards` is the dedicated Whiteboards app. It is a Next App Router
source that runs on TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void behind
[`@tuturuuu/start-bridge`](/build/devops/start-bridge), generated with the
[conversion codemod](/build/devops/start-bridge-codemod). There is no legacy
Vercel project and no legacy subdomain Worker: this app was carved out of Web's
`/[wsId]/whiteboards` routes, so Web keeps serving boards until the mount is
live.

## What moved and what stayed

| Piece | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Board list and board pages, create/edit dialogs, editor shell | `apps/whiteboards` |
| Editor, snapshot format, realtime transport | `packages/whiteboard` (unchanged) |
| Client for the board API | `packages/internal-api/src/whiteboards.ts` |
| Board API (`GET/POST /whiteboards`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /whiteboards/<id>`, `image-url`) | `apps/web` (the list `GET` is new) |
| Realtime checkpoint (`/api/v1/realtime/whiteboard/checkpoint`) | `apps/web` (unchanged) |

The app owns only the satellite shell routes (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/build-info`,
avatar and AI-credit routes, `/api/workspaces/<id>`). Every other `/api/*`
request is forwarded to the central Web API, so no catch-all page exists under
`[locale]/[wsId]`. The actor is `getSatelliteAppSessionUser('whiteboards')`.

## Worker profiles

| Profile | Selected by | Worker | Hosts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Staging (default) | no variable | the staging name in `cloudflare/deployment-profile.mjs` | the root host only, `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1` |
| Production | `VITE_WHITEBOARDS_NATIVE_PROFILE=production` | `tuturuuu-whiteboards` | the root host plus `tuturuuu.com/whiteboards` and `/whiteboards/*` |

`cloudflare/deployment-profile.mjs` holds the names and variables for
`void.config.ts`. `scripts/ci/whiteboards-native-artifact.py`, the runtime test
and `scripts/ci/wave1-native-profiles.json` repeat them, and
`scripts/ci/whiteboards-native-artifact.test.py` pins the artifact script to the
profile. Change them together.
Neither profile declares routes, custom domains, `workers_dev` or `preview_urls`.

- Entry: `cloudflare/worker.ts` (generated); app-owned options in
  `start-bridge.config.ts` (nonce CSP, report-only Trusted Types, the shared
  response policy).
- Binding: `ASSETS` (static output, `run_worker_first`).
- Variable (name): `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX`; optional `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN`
  (default `https://tuturuuu.com`).
- Secrets (names only, set in the Worker): `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`,
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`,
  `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`.
- Data: no database writes and no migrations.

The editor needs no new response-policy exceptions. Trusted Types stays in
report mode (`TTR_TRUSTED_TYPES_WHITEBOARDS` unset or `report`) until a
signed-in crawl of the editor shows no violations; moving it to `enforce` is a
separate reviewed change.

## Build and qualification

`whiteboards-cloudflare.yaml` runs the reusable native workflow (build, routes,
types, unit tests, emitted-Worker runtime, sealed restore) and a
`whiteboards-cutover-artifact` job that builds the production profile, seals the
route-free archive and repeats `test:runtime` from a clean restore. Do not run
`build:cloudflare` on a shared development machine; use the workflow.

```bash
node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/cli.mjs whiteboards          # dry run, never --apply again
python3 scripts/ci/whiteboards-native-artifact.test.py
CI=true bun run --cwd apps/whiteboards test:runtime              # CI only, after the build
```

`scripts/ci/wave1-native-profiles.json` carries the production recipe
(`productionOnly`, secrets, smoke cases) used by `wave1-native-production.yaml`.
Do not re-run the codemod with `--apply`: `void.config.ts`,
`start-bridge.config.ts` and the workflow carry the profile selection by hand.

## Cutover order

The Web redirect and the gateway mount are held commits, separate from the app,
so the product keeps working until the app is live. Each step is verified before the next, and each has a reverse.

1. **Land the app** (source, registries, docs, and the migration
   `20261125130000_whiteboards_cross_app_token_audience.sql`, which adds
   `whiteboards` to `private.cross_app_internal_app_names()` so Web can mint and
   verify cross-app tokens for it; production applies it through the gated
   workflow after the production sync, and sign-in through the app's own host
   waits for that apply). Web's pages are unchanged and
   no gateway route exists. The launcher and the Apps catalog list Whiteboards at
   `whiteboards.tuturuuu.com`, so do step 2 straight after this lands.
2. **Publish the sealed production artifact** from the exact release SHA:
   provision the four Worker secrets first, upload the route-free
   `tuturuuu-whiteboards` build, then attach `whiteboards.tuturuuu.com` to it so
   the launcher link works. Record the Worker version.
3. **Signed-in crawl** of the board list and one editor session through a
   `Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides` staged version; check realtime
   (two members on one board), image upload and the Trusted Types report log.
4. **Mount.** Land the held gateway commit (`/whiteboards`, `/whiteboards/*` in
   `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS`, the `MOUNT_WHITEBOARDS` service binding,
   `/whiteboards` in `PENDING_WEB_MOUNTS` and the redirect Worker's
   `APP_WHITEBOARDS` binding) in the same window as the gateway write. Its
   Wrangler digests in `scripts/ci/wrangler-usage-allowlist.json` need a fresh
   admission with it. Then run `node scripts/active-app-mounts.mjs --live <version.json>`.
5. **Web redirect.** Land the held Web commit: `/[wsId]/whiteboards[/...]`
   redirects to the app, Web's sidebar entry links to it, and Web's copies of
   the pages, adapters and hook are deleted. Landing this before step 4 would
   send members to a path that is not live.
6. **Active mount.** Remove `/whiteboards` from `PENDING_WEB_MOUNTS` in a
   separate change after signed-in acceptance, so Web's logins use the mount.
7. **Subdomain.** Move `whiteboards.tuturuuu.com` from the app Worker to the
   redirect Worker and add `whiteboards` to `SUBDOMAIN_REDIRECT_APPS` so it
   answers 301 to `tuturuuu.com/whiteboards`. Without that list entry the
   `APP_WHITEBOARDS` binding is a pass-through to the app Worker.

## Smoke checks after the mount is live

```bash
curl -sI https://tuturuuu.com/whiteboards/api/build-info       # 200, JSON, no-store
curl -sI https://tuturuuu.com/whiteboards/personal              # 307 to the sign-in page when signed out
curl -sI https://tuturuuu.com/personal/whiteboards              # redirect to /whiteboards/personal
curl -sI https://whiteboards.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info        # 200 until step 7, then 301
```

No smoke request may return `5xx`.

## Rollback

1. Revert the Web commit: boards are served from Web again.
2. Remove the `/whiteboards` entries and the `MOUNT_WHITEBOARDS` binding from the
   gateway (the one-step mount rollback) and re-run the live-mount check.
3. Move `whiteboards.tuturuuu.com` back to the app Worker if step 7 ran. The
   Worker and its versions can stay; nothing else depends on them.

Boards, snapshots and images live in the same tables and bucket as before, so a
rollback touches no data.
